strategy.summary: Reproduce issue #9323 / PR #9390: UECM.from_ardl(...).fit().resid is computed from the wrong endog (ARDL levels) minus UECM fitted values (differences), so it does not match ARDL residuals. The project's own added test test_resids_ardl_uecm in statsmodels/tsa/ardl/tests/test_ardl.py builds an ARDL and a UECM on dane_data with the same lags and asserts assert_allclose(uecm_res.resid, ardl_res.resid). It should fail on buggy d0da572b061f and pass on the fixed revision. The context's test_command (flake8 on the diff) is a style check and cannot exhibit this numerical bug, so it is replaced here.
strategy.reproducing_test: def test_resids_ardl_uecm(): ardl_mod = ARDL(dane_data.lrm, 3, dane_data[["lry","ibo","ide"]], {"lry":1,"ibo":3,"ide":2}); ardl_res = ardl_mod.fit(); uecm_mod = UECM(dane_data.lrm, 3, dane_data[["lry","ibo","ide"]], {"lry":1,"ibo":3,"ide":2}); uecm_res = uecm_mod.fit(); assert_allclose(uecm_res.resid, ardl_res.resid)
strategy.success_criterion: Transition: on buggy d0da572b061f the test FAILS because uecm_res.resid is built from ARDL levels minus UECM differenced fitted values, so assert_allclose reports a shape or value mismatch against ardl_res.resid. On the fixed revision, where UECM results define resid as model._y minus fittedvalues, the test PASSES at assert_allclose default tolerance.
strategy.numerical_probe: Compare uecm_res.resid with ardl_res.resid for the dane_data ARDL(3; lry 1, ibo 3, ide 2) specification, checking shape and values at default rtol.

input_output_examples.input: ardl = sm.tsa.ARDL(S[:,[0]], 1, S[:,[1]], 1); ardlfit = ardl.fit(); uecm = sm.tsa.UECM.from_ardl(ardl); uecmfit = uecm.fit(); uecmfit.resid
input_output_examples.buggy_output: residuals computed by subtracting UECM fitted values (differences) from ARDL endogenous values (levels)
input_output_examples.expected_output: ardlfit.resid (the same residuals as the equivalent ARDL model)

The developer's test uses dane_data and UECM directly rather than UECM.from_ardl; the from_ardl path in the issue example is not covered by that test, so a separate check using UECM.from_ardl may be needed to confirm the issue's exact trigger.

Dependency versions are unbounded in the evidence (statsmodels and flake8 constraints null, python_version null); the strategy leaves versions unpinned and relies on the buggy revision's own build requirements, which were not provided.
The build must be done from source (C/Cython extensions); a stale or prebuilt wheel of a different revision would not reproduce the bug.

Nothing in the evidence ties this defect to a specific platform, compiler, BLAS, or thread setting, so no platform-specific behaviour is assumed; if the test fails to transition on a given machine, check that fit results are not dependent on optimizer or BLAS differences.
The PR diff also contains unrelated formatting changes in test_ardl.py and test_var_jmulti.py; they do not affect the reproducing test.
The issue sample uses unseeded random data; the developer test uses dane_data, which is deterministic, so no seed is needed for this test.

oracle.reference_source: ardl_res.resid from ARDL fit on the same data and lags
oracle.why: The issue states UECM residuals should equal ARDL residuals since no transformation is applied, so the reference is the ARDL residual series at default assert_allclose tolerance.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On the buggy revision uecm_res.resid subtracts UECM fitted values (in differences) from ARDL levels, so it does not match ardl_res.resid; assert_allclose raises an AssertionError on the shape or value mismatch.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision UECM resid is model._y minus fittedvalues, which matches ARDL residuals within default assert_allclose tolerance, so the test passes.
